chunks: Muhammad narrated from Humayd ibn al-Ziyad, from al-Hasan ibn Muhammad al-Kindi, from Ahmad ibn al-Hasan al-Mithamī, from Aban ibn Uthman, from Abu al-Abbas, who said:

I said to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him): A man guaranteed for another man the person of a third party, saying: 'If I bring him to you, and if not, five hundred dirhams are upon me.' He (the Imam) said: 'The guarantee of the person is upon him, and no dirhams are upon him.' Then he said: 'Five hundred dirhams are upon me if I do not deliver him to you.' He (the Imam) said: 'The dirhams are binding upon him if he does not deliver him to you.'

key_terms.بِنَفْسِ رَجُلٍ: for the person of a man (personal guarantee)
key_terms.كَفَلَ: to guarantee or take responsibility for

ai.seo_question: What is the difference between guaranteeing a person and guaranteeing a debt in Islamic law?
ai.summary: This narration from Shaykh al-Tusi’s *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* elucidates the principle of *al-kafalah bi al-nafs* (guarantee of a person), highlighting the juristic distinction between a guarantee of presence and a monetary debt. It establishes that a penalty is not automatically attached to the guarantee unless explicitly conditioned, reflecting the Shia emphasis on precise contractual stipulations (*shurut*) in civil transactions. This ruling underscores the flexibility in personal guarantees, allowing the guarantor to bear only the person's liability unless a specific financial undertaking is verbally or contractually bound.
